subject: simsem a priori power analysis, coverage issues for latent dependent variables

messages.author: 999e6e262ffc2d33
messages.subject: simsem a priori power analysis, coverage issues for latent dependent variables
parts:
Hello!

I am trying to conduct an a priori power analysis using simsem, but am running into problems with regards to coverage values.
I defined my population values using library(simstandard), as such:

m <- "
#measurament model
ATT =~ 0.82*att1 + 0.82*att2 + 0.82*att3 + 0.82*att4 + 0.82*att6 + 0.82*att7
SN =~ 0.82*sn1 + 0.82*sn2 + 0.82*sn5
PBC =~ 0.85*pbc1 + 0.85*pbc2 + 0.85*pbc3 + 0.85*pbc4 + 0.85*pbc5
INT =~ 0.70*int1 + 0.70*int3 + 0.70*int4 + 0.70*int5
CERT =~ 0.75*cert1 + 0.75*cert2 + 0.75*cert3 + 0.75*cert4
SEV =~ 0.75*ps1 + 0.75*ps2 + 0.75*ps3
#structural model
ATT ~ (-0.15)*CERT + (-0.15)*SEV
INT ~ 0.35*ATT + 0.2*SN + 0.40*PBC  
#covariances
SN ~~ 0.40*PBC
SN ~~ (-0.30)*CERT
SN ~~ (-0.35)*SEV
PBC ~~ (-0.35)*CERT
PBC ~~ (-0.35)*SEV
CERT ~~ 0.50*SEV
"
m_complete <- model_complete(m)
cat(m_complete)

#This gave me the following values for my population model:

PopMod <- '
#measurament model
ATT =~ 0.82*att1 + 0.82*att2 + 0.82*att3 + 0.82*att4 + 0.82*att6 + 0.82*att7
SN =~ 0.82*sn1 + 0.82*sn2 + 0.82*sn5
PBC =~ 0.85*pbc1 + 0.85*pbc2 + 0.85*pbc3 + 0.85*pbc4 + 0.85*pbc5
INT =~ 0.70*int1 + 0.70*int3 + 0.70*int4 + 0.70*int5
CERT =~ 0.75*cert1 + 0.75*cert2 + 0.75*cert3 + 0.75*cert4
SEV =~ 0.75*ps1 + 0.75*ps2 + 0.75*ps3

#structural model
ATT ~ (-0.15)*CERT + (-0.15)*SEV
INT ~ 0.35*ATT + 0.2*SN + 0.40*PBC 

SN ~~ 0.40*PBC
SN ~~ (-0.30)*CERT
SN ~~ (-0.35)*SEV
PBC ~~ (-0.35)*CERT
PBC ~~ (-0.35)*SEV
CERT ~~ 0.50*SEV

# Variances
att1 ~~ 0.3276 * att1
att2 ~~ 0.3276 * att2
att3 ~~ 0.3276 * att3
att4 ~~ 0.3276 * att4
att6 ~~ 0.3276 * att6
att7 ~~ 0.3276 * att7
sn1 ~~ 0.3276 * sn1
sn2 ~~ 0.3276 * sn2
sn5 ~~ 0.3276 * sn5
pbc1 ~~ 0.2775 * pbc1
pbc2 ~~ 0.2775 * pbc2
pbc3 ~~ 0.2775 * pbc3
pbc4 ~~ 0.2775 * pbc4
pbc5 ~~ 0.2775 * pbc5
int1 ~~ 0.51 * int1
int3 ~~ 0.51 * int3
int4 ~~ 0.51 * int4
int5 ~~ 0.51 * int5
cert1 ~~ 0.4375 * cert1
cert2 ~~ 0.4375 * cert2
cert3 ~~ 0.4375 * cert3
cert4 ~~ 0.4375 * cert4
ps1 ~~ 0.4375 * ps1
ps2 ~~ 0.4375 * ps2
ps3 ~~ 0.4375 * ps3
ATT ~~ 0.9325 * ATT # THIS CAUSES PROBLEMS (see below)
SN ~~ 1 * SN
PBC ~~ 1 * PBC
INT ~~ 0.57045 * INT # THIS CAUSES PROBLEMS (see below)
CERT ~~ 1 * CERT
SEV ~~ 1 * SEV
'
#My analysis model was defined as such:

mod.analysis <- '
ATT =~ att1 + att2 + att3 + att4 + att6 + att7
SN =~ sn1 + sn2 + sn5
PBC=~ pbc1 + pbc2 + pbc3 + pbc4 + pbc5
INT =~ int1 + int3 + int4 + int5
CERT =~ cert1 + cert2 + cert3 + cert4
SEV =~ ps1 + ps2 + ps3

INT~ ATT+SN+PBC
ATT~CERT+SEV

SN ~~ PBC
SN ~~ CERT
SN ~~ SEV
PBC ~~ CERT
PBC ~~ SEV
CERT ~~ SEV
'

Output <- simsem::sim(nRep=500
                      n=870,
                      model = mod.analysis,
                      generate=PopMod,
                      std.lv=TRUE,
                      lavaanfun = "sem")
round(summaryParam(Output, alpha=0.05, detail=TRUE), digits=3)


If i define my two latent dependent variables as above:
ATT ~~ 0.9325 * ATT
INT ~~ 0.57045 * INT,
the coverage for their respective parts of the model (ATT =~ ... and INT =~) in the simsem output becomes 0 or close to 0.

Am I doing something wrong? As I understood the theory behind simsem, i need to define the residual values for dependent variables like this.

On the other hand, I obtained multiple published papers that utilized simsem to run a priori power analyses and in them they did not define their dependent latent variables to reflect the residual unexplained values like I did, they defined them (using the my model as an example) as such:
ATT ~~ 1 * ATT
INT ~~ 1* INT,

When I also do this, my simsem coverage gets above 0.9 for their respective measurement parts of the model.

Can you provide advice:
a) what am I doing wrong?
b) what is the correct way to define this part of the population model?

Thank you in advance.

Kind regards,

Miljan

messages.author: f6d12b388faad456
messages.subject: Re: simsem a priori power analysis, coverage issues for latent dependent variables
parts:
Hi, Miljan.

When you set std.lv = TRUE, you are saying that the latent variables have all mean = 0 and variance = 1, what is not true in your population model.
However, in your case, it is not true because ATT and INT are endogenous variables, do your population variance is the residual variance, and I am not sure whether simsem/lavaan understand the difference between total and residual variance when you use std.lv = TRUE . My guess is that they don’t.

So, I believe you’ll need to write the population model using unstandardized coefficients — i.e., the identification of the model will be done by fixing the first factor loading of each factor to 1. Or you’ll have to compute the power for these parameters manually using simsem output.

Best,
Yago
